title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1LC1RE_1LF0RA_1LA1LD_1RC0RE_---1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1LC1RE_1LF0RA_1LA1LD_1RC0RE_---1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The tape is made of the words 10 and 1110 (runs of one or three 1s, each followed by a single 0), with a few longer runs of 1s; at the left end it begins with a run of 11010 (7 copies around step 1.9·109) followed by one long run of 1s (47 of them). Both ends grow logarithmically. No exact rule has been found.
verdict: The question is open. 49 event rules, proved in Lean for every size, cover 65,854,171 of the 65,868,043 visits of the head to cell −134 in state E in the first 3·109 steps (99.98%); none of them halts (each ends at the next event). Every halt passes through 0 C> 0 (from the table; from there it halts, Lean halt_ctx), which never occurs in 3·109 steps; C read a 0 with a 1 on its left only 25 times, 19 before the first event and 6 in the 13,872 uncovered events.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 298 cells have been visited and 182 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.102). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.037).

claims.title: The halt from the halting context
claims.text: From 0 C> 0 the machine reaches its halting transition (proved step by step, then step_none_iff). The halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from C reading a 0 (C writes 1 and moves left), so the machine halts exactly when C reads a 0 with a 0 on its left. Lean (halt_ctx) proves only that from this context the machine halts; that every halt passes through it is read off the table, not proved in Lean.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: 10 shift rules over the words of the tape (for example (01)^n C> 0 becomes C> 0 (11)^n in 4n steps and C> (100)^n becomes (111)^n C> in 3n steps), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 20,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the visited tape is 314 cells wide and holds 194 ones.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps C read a 1 with a 0 on its left 110 times and a 0 with a 1 on its left 25 times (the last at step 695,839,958, at a new right cell); it never read a 0 with a 0 on its left.

claims.title: Growth
claims.text: Both ends grow logarithmically: each new cell takes a roughly constant factor more time.

claims.title: 49 event rules for every size
claims.text: From an event (E on cell −134) to the next: the 8-step event x 0 0 E> 0 1 1 1 → x 1 1 E> 0 1 0 1, and the long event that turns a run of a+1 ones left of the head into 1 1 1 0 0^a and rewrites the 01 words on the right into 0111 words (2a + 18 steps and up, for every a and any tape beyond), in all the right-hand shapes that occur. Mined from the run by the batch's py/miner.py.

claims.title: Coverage: 99.98% of the events
claims.text: 65,868,043 events in 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, 13,872 not matched by a rule.

claims.title: 0 C> 0 never occurs
claims.text: In 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps C never reads a 0 with a 0 on its left; it reads a 0 with a 1 on its left 25 times: 19 before the first event and 6 inside uncovered events, none inside a proved rule.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs C on a 0 with a 0 on its left; the words 10 and 1110 never put two 0s side by side, so only the irregular places (the ends, the long runs) could; without the rule of the counter this is not proved.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The head works at one cell, alternating a short event with a long one that clears a run of 1s on the left and rewrites words on the right; all but 0.02% of these events follow rules proved for every size. The one way to stop has never come up.

facts.text: Event rules proved in Lean for every size.
Of the 65,868,043 events of 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps follow them.
From it the machine halts (Lean halt_ctx); every halt passes through it (from the table).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.102). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.037).
After 109 steps the tape spans 298 cells (191 left of the start, 56 right), with a density of 1s of 0.611.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A short event and a long one
html: Watch the head on cell −134 in state E (an event; 15,346,830 of them in steps 2.5–3·109). Most events are of two kinds. The short one (8 steps): x 0 0 E> 0 1 1 1 becomes x 1 1 E> 0 1 0 1. The long one: a run of a+1 ones just left of the head becomes 1 1 1 0 0…0, and the 01 words to the right become 0111 words, in 2a + 18 steps or more. The rules hold for every a.
Early in the run (to step 8.5·108) the busiest point was D on cell −108; the same rules, read at cell −134, cover those events too.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: 49 rules, each proved in Lean for every value of its repeat counts, match all but 13,872 of the 65,868,043 events of the first 3·109 steps. None of them halts. The machine halts after 0 C> 0, which never happened; its nearest relative 1 C> 0 happened 25 times, never inside a proved rule.

sections.heading: The one way to stop
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from C reading a 0 (C writes 1 and moves left), so the machine halts exactly when C reads a 0 with a 0 on its left. So the machine halts exactly when it produces 0 C> 0; Lean proves the steps from there to the halt (halt_ctx).
How close does it come? What C has ahead of it, counted at every step of the first 109 steps:

In the first 109 steps C read a 1 with a 0 on its left 110 times and a 0 with a 1 on its left 25 times (the last at step 695,839,958, at a new right cell); it never read a 0 with a 0 on its left.

sections.heading: What remains open
html: Read the rules as a macro machine (what the run of 1s and the right words count), decode the 13,872 uncovered events (left-end visits and layout changes), and prove that C never meets 0 0.

summary: One engine (E on cell -134) alternates an 8-step event with one that turns a run of 1s on its left into 0s and rewrites 10-words into 1110-words on its right; 49 event rules proved for all sizes cover 99.98% of 6.6·10^7 events in 3·10^9 steps; 0 C> 0 (from it the machine halts) never occurs.
